**h01** — **Component:** `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`), whose `CheckAndPresign` re-presigns S3 attachment URLs and writes the new `Reference` + `LastPresignedTime` back via `Store.UpdateAttachment` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:47-132`). — **Schedule:** once at startup, then every 12 h (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`; ticker loop `:29-41`); it re-signs only URLs within 4 days of the 5-day presign expiry (`:85-91`, expiry set at `internal/storage/s3/s3.go:79`). — **Wiring:** `Server.startBackgroundRunners` — `server/server.go:162-171` (immediate `RunOnce` at `server/server.go:163`, goroutine `Run` at `:169`), called from `Server.Start` (`server/server.go:129`).

**h02** — **Delivery function:** `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120-180` (the `safeClient.Do(req)` at `:152`); it is fed asynchronously by `webhook.PostAsync` → `asyncPostQueue` → 4 worker goroutines (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55, 184-196`). — **Protection:** dial-time SSRF guard — `safeClient`'s custom `Transport.DialContext = safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`), which resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`) using `isReservedIP` over `reservedCIDRs` (loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.0.0/16 IMDS, IPv6 equivalents) — `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-54`. Because the check happens at dial time it also defeats DNS rebinding. A second, config-time check is `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62-83`), used by `CreateUserWebhook`/`UpdateUserWebhook` (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`). The escape hatch `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`) is never set in non-test code, so it defaults to false.

**h03** — **Abstraction package:** `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:3-8`, `IdentityProviderUserInfo`); the provider config union lives in `storepb.IdentityProvider` (`proto/gen/store/idp.pb.go`). — **Implementation package:** `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:19-42`, `IdentityProvider` with `NewIdentityProvider`/`ExchangeToken`/`UserInfo`), OAuth2/OIDC being the only concrete protocol shipped; it is used from `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go`.

**h04** — **No.** `mysql.NewDB` is referenced exactly once in the whole repo: the driver-selection switch in `NewDBDriver` at `store/db/db.go:22`. Evidence: `grep -rn "mysql.NewDB" --include=*.go .` returns only that line (no test file constructs it either). Test infrastructure only starts a MySQL *container* (`store/test/containers.go:101-105`, testcontainers `mysql.Run`), not the driver type. By contrast `sqlite.NewDB` is also called directly in tests (`store/deployment_config_test.go:416`, `store/demo_seed_test.go:24`).

**h05** — **Mechanism:** explicit Go code, per-driver, inside the delete-user transaction — not a DB rule. Two deletions run: reactions *on the user's memos* (`deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`) and reactions *authored by the user* (`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`).
- `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96,102` (impls at `:380-390`, `:400-402`)
- `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102` (impls at `:380`, `:400`)
- `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102` (impls at `:417`, `:437`)
- Entry point `Store.DeleteUser` → `driver.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171-180`).

**Evidence there is no DB-level rule:** the `reaction` table is declared with no foreign keys in any dialect — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:91-99`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:90-98`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:90-98`; the only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the current schema is `memo_share.memo_id → memo.id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109` and peers).

---

**r01** — **Premise is wrong on both counts: there is no Redis anywhere in this codebase** (no `redis` dependency in `go.mod`/`go.sum`, no match for "redis" in any source file), **and there is no per-entity TTL configuration for users.** The actual mechanism is a process-local in-memory cache: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` backed by `sync.Map`, TTL + `MaxItems` eviction + a cleanup goroutine). The `Store` holds three of them — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — all built with one shared config at `store/store.go:37-52`: `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`. So user entries expire 10 minutes after write, keyed by user ID (`userCacheKey`, `store/user.go:88`); they are also refreshed on every `CreateUser`/`UpdateUser`/`ListUsers`/`GetUser` (`store/user.go:99,121,133,142,166`) and invalidated on delete (`store/user.go:178`). Cache lookup only happens when querying by ID (`store/user.go:149-156`); lookups by username go straight to the driver.

**r02** — **Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase** — no per-user limiter, no limiter of any kind, and therefore no request limits. Searching for `ratelimit|rate limit|limiter|throttle` across `server/`, `internal/`, `store/`, `cmd/` yields exactly one hit, and it is an aspirational comment in a doc file: `internal/email/doc.go:86` ("Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse"). No `golang.org/x/time/rate` or equivalent dependency is present. What the request path actually has: Echo's `Recover` and CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`), Connect interceptors (`server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`) with auth/ACL enforcement driven by `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` and `authz.go`, plus a concurrency semaphore for thumbnail generation (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:107,116`) — which bounds parallel work, not request rate.

**r03** — **Premise is wrong: no nightly database-cleanup job exists, and no cron scheduler is running.** There are zero registered cron jobs and zero scheduled times to report. `internal/scheduler` (a cron-expression parser and job runner: `parser.go`, `job.go`, `scheduler.go`, `middleware.go`) is dead code at this commit — the only importers of `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler` are its own tests (`internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`, `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`); no production file imports it, and `scheduler.New` is never called from `server/` or `cmd/`. The only recurring background work is the S3 presign runner on a plain 12-hour `time.Ticker` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27-41`), started at `server/server.go:162-171` — that is a URL-refresh task, not a cleanup, and it is not cron-scheduled.

**r04** — **Premise is wrong: neither NATS nor RabbitMQ is used — there is no external message broker at all, and no queue is declared anywhere.** No `nats`, `amqp`, `rabbitmq`, or `kafka` dependency appears in `go.mod`/`go.sum`. The actual mechanism is a purely in-process, in-memory queue: a buffered Go channel `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`), drained by 4 worker goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `webhook.Post` (`:120`). Producers call `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184-196`), which does a non-blocking send and **drops** the event with a warning when the buffer is full (`:189-195`). Consequences worth noting: no durability, no retries, and no cross-instance delivery — the queue dies with the process.

**r05** — **Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema, server, or dependency in this repository** (zero matches for "graphql" in any `.go`, `go.mod`, or `package.json` file). The actual public API surface is Protobuf/gRPC-defined, in `proto/api/v1/`, generated into `proto/gen/api/v1/`:
- **Connect-RPC** handlers — `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/*.connect.go`, registered via `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go` and `connect_services.go`
- **REST/JSON via grpc-gateway** — `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go`, mounted by `apiV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/server.go:88`)
- Plus non-RPC HTTP surfaces: the file server `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), SSE (`server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), MCP (`server/router/mcp/service.go`, `server/server.go:92-96`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:67`).

Services defined: `MemoService`, `UserService`, `AuthService`, `AttachmentService`, `ShortcutService`, `InstanceService`, `IdpService`, `AIService`.
